Hello, the first time I went he seemed friendly, which makes sense if he wants to sell something, but the second time the conversation veered off into the Yugoslav Wars, yes, friends, and all because I was talking about legality, specifically about HHC and its legality in Spain. I quote his exact words: "What do you young people know? I was in the war, what are you going to tell me? You're not going to lecture me on morality" (in a very unpleasant tone). I was hoping to buy something, but when he saw I looked like a young Vox supporter, he got carried away and launched into a speech I didn't understand, since I'm not a Vox supporter and we were only talking about the legality of HHC.

Any young person looking for CBD options in Nigrán, Coruxo, San Miguel, or Canido might get lucky one day, but this is what's behind the counter.

one_star_reviews.text:
Disappointing stay — particularly the location and service

I stayed at Stephouse Pozuelo while attending a conference at UCM Somosaguas. Although the property may appear convenient because it is relatively close to the university campus, after my experience I would actually recommend conference attendees consider staying around Gran Vía, Sol, or another central Madrid location instead. Central Madrid gives you much easier access to restaurants, shopping, entertainment and, importantly, far better public transport connections.

Getting between Pozuelo and central Madrid was one of the biggest inconveniences of my stay. Public transport to and from Moncloa largely depends on buses such as 657, 657A and 658A, and the intervals can sometimes be quite long. This makes the location inconvenient if you want to move around Madrid efficiently, particularly in the evening or when you are working to a schedule. I ended up feeling unnecessarily isolated from the city.

Unfortunately, the check-in experience was also very poor. I arrived at approximately 3 PM on 31 August, which was the stated check-in time, and I was the only guest checking in at that moment. Despite there being no queue, the process took around 30 minutes before I could access my accommodation. I can only imagine how long this might take during a busy check-in period.

Communication was another challenge. The staff member assisting me spoke very limited English, which made an already lengthy process more difficult. I understand that I am visiting Spain and do not expect everyone to speak fluent English, but for accommodation serving international guests, there should be a workable way to communicate basic check-in information and resolve problems. I also felt that my frustration about the unusually long check-in process was met somewhat defensively rather than with an attempt to acknowledge or resolve the issue.

One interaction in particular left a very poor impression. Later, I approached a male staff member who was standing directly in front of me and using the computer at reception because I had a question. He looked at me and simply told me that his shift was over. I understand completely that staff should not be expected to work after their shift, but from a guest’s perspective this was an extraordinarily unhelpful response. If you are still behind reception and interacting with the reception computer, it is reasonable for a guest to assume that you are available. At minimum, he could simply have directed me to the colleague who was on duty rather than dismissing the question.

Another important issue is the room description. The apartment I stayed in actually contained two bedrooms, which was not made sufficiently clear in the room information when I booked. Accommodation layout—particularly whether spaces are shared with another occupant—is basic information that guests should be able to understand clearly before making a reservation.

Overall, the accommodation itself was adequate, but the combination of the isolated location, inconvenient transport, extremely slow check-in, communication difficulties, unclear room information and disappointing customer service made the experience much less comfortable than it should have been.

If I were attending another conference at UCM Somosaguas, I personally would not stay here again. I would stay in central Madrid and commute to the university instead.

I hereby formally file a complaint regarding the events that occurred at the gym.

I subsequently had to go to the emergency room on my own, where I received treatment. I have the corresponding medical report that confirms this treatment.

There were also eyewitnesses to the events, whose information I can provide if necessary.

In addition, I was charged twice for my gym membership, a situation I have also disputed and which should be refunded.

Therefore, I request:

1. A refund of the amount charged twice.

2. A refund of the corresponding membership fee, taking into account the events and the resulting situation. 3. A written explanation of the staff's actions during the incident.

4. That any security camera footage from the day and time of the incident be preserved, as it may be relevant to clarifying what happened.

I reserve the right to take appropriate legal action for the assault, threats, and damages caused, as well as to provide the emergency room report and witness statements.

I request a written response to this complaint.

one_star_reviews.text:
I was very disappointed with the service I received at Le Petit Rose, a nail salon in Cánovas del Castillo (Valladolid).

I had a pedicure appointment booked over a month ago for 5:30 pm with Paula. I was shocked to learn that Paula no longer worked there and that Míchel would be seeing me instead—a change that no one had bothered to inform me about beforehand.

When I found out, I called to cancel and try to book an appointment with Lucía, but she was on vacation. I finally confirmed that I would still come to my appointment, accepting the change of professional.

I left work and took the bus. Due to a delay, I arrived at 5:40 pm, 10 minutes late.

Míchel herself greeted me and told me she couldn't see me because she had another client afterward. There was no alternative, no suggestion of finding another time slot, no new appointment, and not the slightest attempt to offer a solution.

I completely understand that schedules must be respected, but respect for other people's time should go both ways. I had been waiting for an appointment with Paula for over a month, and the center didn't even bother to inform me that she no longer worked there. Even so, I accepted the change, confirmed I would attend, and went directly from work.

After the center's lack of communication, I expected at least a little understanding regarding a 10-minute delay and, above all, some willingness to find an alternative.

I don't plan to return to Le Petit Rose, and certainly, after the way I was treated, I wouldn't put myself in Míchel's hands again. For me, customer service is also part of being a good professional.

one_star_reviews.text: Beware of this shameless con artist. I was interested in a car, he sent me a video, and it didn't look bad. The first thing he told me was that he would send me the car and that I had 15 days to test drive it, and if I didn't like it, I could return it. He said the car was fine, that it would be delivered with all the maintenance done and cleaned. Well, after 20 days of making the bank transfer, the car arrived on a tow truck, and it was a disaster, full of dents, cracked tires, and missing parts that weren't shown in the video—in short, terrible. I called him while the car was still on the tow truck and told him I didn't want the car in that condition, and he said he wouldn't return it and immediately blocked me on his phone. The tow truck driver had to leave, and he had to drop off the car, and since I couldn't contact him, we decided to take it out. To my surprise, the car wouldn't even start, and on top of that, it didn't have a drop of diesel in it. Inside, there were no documents of any kind, just dirt and cigarette butts. I managed to contact him via WhatsApp, and he told me the paperwork would arrive in a few days and that he wasn't returning the car. Tired of waiting, after two months I decided to do a little research and discovered that the car had a lien and couldn't be transferred. I contacted him again via WhatsApp, and he said he didn't know and gave me a bunch of excuses, all of which were lies. I then contacted the Civil Guard, who gave him a hard time. It took five months before he sent me the paperwork, but I still haven't seen the vehicle registration document; I'll have to request a duplicate myself. So, I bought the car because I needed it and couldn't move it from my house due to the lack of documents. Of course, it hadn't had any maintenance done. I had to replace all four tires because it was dangerous, change the oil and filters, replace the gearshift, and replace the rearview mirror. It didn't even have air conditioning or floor mats. My advice is: don't buy anything here. I'm giving it one star because I can't give it five.

one_star_reviews.text:
A significant doctrinal shift worth noting.

In September 2026, Jehovah's Witnesses officially announced a change in their stance on blood components. Currently, the acceptance of red blood cells, white blood cells, plasma, and platelets is left to each individual's conscience. The refusal to receive whole blood, according to the same announcement, remains in place.

This contrasts with the position previously taught. For example, the 1994 issue of Awake! featured the series "Young People Who Put God First," and the organization's official library also includes articles from that period about young people who opposed transfusions.

Therefore, there is a fact that anyone can verify directly in their own publications: the official position on certain blood components has changed over time.

The question I consider legitimate is: what were the consequences of the decisions made when the previous position was in effect?

I believe this is an important enough topic that those familiar with this organization should have access to both its current position and what was taught previously, so they can draw their own conclusions.

one_star_reviews.text: Discrimination at the Civic Center Campus due to his disability by the campus organizer and the Director of the Civic Centers of Santander. I waited a few weeks to see if there would be any sign of empathy, but seeing that the level is so low, I'm leaving a review. I took my son to the English campus at the center in August. The first week my son (who has ASD/ADHD) was fine except for a few isolated incidents. The following week, new children arrived, and my son had some arguments and run-ins with some of them. The organizer (English School America academy) called me, and the conversation was polite but also humiliating for a parent with a child with difficulties. There's only one teacher with 12 children, and he has to take care of your son, leaving the others unattended. We're afraid he might hit someone because he's 11 years old. The director of the Civic Centers called me; she's afraid something serious might happen, etc. My response was, "What do you want me to tell him?" Well... Yes, the boy can't attend to him. To make matters worse, I told him I paid €190 for the one-month camp; the camp has different prices depending on whether you go for 1, 2, 3, or 4 weeks. He refunded me €70, as if I had booked two weeks for €120 (plus, he only went for three days because they asked him to leave). He says no, then to top it all off, I see that his status shows a picture of the Palestinian flag with a tree growing. Anyway, I'm supporting the Palestinian cause from 4,000 km away on my sofa, but then I discriminate against an 11-year-old boy with difficulties just 300 meters away. That's the low level of education, and they hire staff for these things at a community center (in theory, we all go there, especially a child). I have to say that I called the general director of the community centers twice. My feeling is that she was aware of everything and that she called the camp manager, who also invited my son to... I told him what I wrote about the money, you're right, it can't be, blah blah blah. I'm still waiting for him to call me.

Today I called to carry out a couple of tasks that they told me I could do through the app, and... first lie, you can't do them through the app.
I called to cancel a service that I was "required" to sign up for (the first 3 months free) and after 28 minutes on the phone and being transferred to 3 different departments... just when they were finally going to cancel that service... the call was cut off, what a coincidence! And the other lie... is that in the contracted plan, I could choose 5 additional days at that price... surprise... no, I can't... because, as they tell me today, a smart service monitors my usage, and when they sent me the contract, they said that 5 days is the best option, and I have 5 days to change them or they stay with those days... this information wasn't mentioned at all during the sign-up call.

I'm trying to file a complaint and have the call recorded... but that's complicated too. What's not complicated is switching companies; thanks for making the decision easier.

Unfortunately, I had a very disappointing experience with this doctor. At my first consultation, I waited around 35 minutes before being seen.

For the first treatment, I had to travel from Sotogrande to La Línea specifically for the appointment. I then waited for approximately one hour, meaning I lost around 2½ hours of my day in total. Despite this, I was given an alternative appointment.

At the alternative appointment, I again waited for more than 30 minutes, but the doctor did not show up at all. I was later told that it was a holiday, which I find particularly frustrating because the appointment had been given to me by the doctor herself.

I understand that schedules can sometimes change and unexpected circumstances can happen, but in my opinion, patients' time should be respected and appointments should be properly communicated if they cannot be kept.

Overall, a very frustrating and disappointing disrespectful experience. I would have expected much better communication and professionalism. I went to Clinica Julia Alvarez it it worked all smoothly.

The story of the L'Hostal de la Grossa is a dark Catalan folktale and urban legend from the Moianès region in Spain. It describes a sinister roadside inn run by murderous hosts.

The Legend of the Trap Bed

The Location: According to local lore, the infamous inn once stood between the towns of Moià and Calders, near an ancient megalithic stone dolmen.

The Target: When the innkeepers suspected an arriving traveler was carrying a large amount of money or valuables, they assigned them a very specific guest room.

The Trap: This room featured a fatal, custom-built bed equipped with a hidden mechanical spring or lever system.

The Killing: Once the unsuspecting guest fell fast asleep, the hosts triggered the mechanism from outside or below. The bed would violently fold inward or snap shut, crushing and suffocating the sleeper to death.

Disposing of the Evidence: To ensure no trace of the victim or the crime ever remained, the murderers disposed of the body by burning it inside the inn's large commercial bread oven.

I took my car in to have the rear brake pads replaced. Once the car was at the garage, they called me to say that the brake discs also needed replacing because, according to them, they were in bad condition.

What surprised me was that just three days earlier, the car had been to another garage where they had already told me the pads needed replacing, but assured me the discs were in perfect condition.

After the replacement, the car started making a lot of noise, not only when braking, but even while driving without pressing the brake pedal, something that didn't happen before, even with the pads practically worn out. I told them about it several times, and the solution they gave me was to bring the car back as soon as possible to have the pads replaced again, claiming they wouldn't work, in addition to replacing the discs.

Faced with this situation, I decided to take it back to the first garage that had given me an estimate so they could look at it. After inspecting it, they informed me that the problem wasn't the discs, as they were in perfect condition, but rather that one of the brake pads wasn't installed correctly.

I think that before recommending such a major parts replacement, they should be absolutely sure what the real problem is. My experience wasn't good, and personally, I won't be taking my car there again.

I don't know if it's due to a lack of knowledge or if they just wanted to rip me off.

The point is, I trusted this garage, and it didn't work out well; I had to go to another garage and pay again.

My Orbea Oiz started having problems from day one. After several checkups at the dealer, Mammoth Bikes, and then sending it to Orbea for repair, the problem persisted without a satisfactory solution.

Before going to court, I tried to resolve it through the usual channels: the Consumer Protection Office and arbitration. When I couldn't get a solution, I finally had to resort to legal action.

After this whole process, the court ruled in my favor.

I'm sharing my experience because I believe it's important for consumers to know their rights and understand that when a product has problems from the start and the usual solutions don't work, we can also turn to the courts.

one_star_reviews.text:
A Complete Disappointment for a €700 Piece of Jewelry

Just a year ago, a friend of mine spent €700 on a PDPAOLA engagement ring. Given its price and what it represents, this piece should offer quality and durability commensurate with the investment.

However, after barely a year, the ring has begun to lose its color and show obvious signs of wear. When I contacted the brand to report the problem, their solution was a rhodium plating. In other words, applying a new coating to disguise the wear, instead of offering a solution that lives up to the expectations of a piece of jewelry at this price.

An engagement ring is not just any accessory. It's a piece of jewelry with enormous sentimental value, purchased with the hope of keeping it for many years, not watching it deteriorate after only one.

The most disappointing thing isn't just the premature wear, but also the brand's response to the problem. When someone pays €700 for a piece of jewelry, they expect quality, durability, and after-sales service that lives up to their expectations.

Personally, I know for sure that I would never choose PDPAOLA for a piece of jewelry intended for such a significant occasion. My friend's experience was enough for me to rule out the brand and not recommend it to anyone looking for jewelry worthy of such a special moment.

To those of you thinking of buying any of their jewelry, I advise you to do your research beforehand and consider whether the quality and after-sales service truly justify the price.

A very disappointing experience that makes me seriously question the brand's value for money.

one_star_reviews.text:
I want to express my complete dissatisfaction with the treatment I received today at the Primaprix store in San Agustín de Guadalix.
I made a considerable purchase: six 2-liter bottles of shower gel, five 1-liter bottles of shampoo, and four bottles of Kallos Kerat shampoo, in addition to other products. Due to the size and weight of the purchase, I asked to use the shopping cart to take it to my car, which was parked directly in front of the store, clearly explaining that I would return it in a few minutes.
The cashier's response, and especially her attitude, was completely unnecessarily cold, rigid, and lacking in empathy. I fully understand that there may be rules regarding the use of shopping carts, and I am not questioning their enforcement. What I find unacceptable is the way I was treated, with absolutely no willingness to find a reasonable solution for a purchase of such size and weight.

Finally, to avoid creating an unpleasant situation in front of other customers, I decided to take the purchase and not return it. However, honestly, I should have returned it, because the way I was treated turned a normal purchase into an absolutely unpleasant experience.

I wasn't expecting any special treatment, just a minimum of courtesy, empathy, and common sense. When a customer has just made a purchase like this and has the vehicle literally in front of them, I believe the situation deserved at least a courteous response and a reasonable alternative, instead of such a cold and uncooperative attitude.

I think this type of behavior directly damages Primaprix's image. A company can have its rules, but the way its employees communicate them is also part of the customer experience.

I hope this complaint is taken into account and that the incident is reviewed, because the problem wasn't the existence of a rule, but the complete lack of empathy and professionalism with which I was made to comply. As a customer, after this experience, I am left with a frankly negative feeling and I consider that the treatment received was totally disproportionate to such a simple situation to resolve.

I completed a course to obtain a professional certificate. After attending and passing all the theoretical modules and completing my practical training, I suffered appendicitis that required emergency surgery and almost two weeks of hospitalization. Despite this being a medical situation completely beyond my control, I was not given the opportunity to make up the remaining practical training. As a result, after having completed almost the entire course, I have been unable to finish it and have not received my certificate.

I find it very unfair that, given my serious medical circumstances, no alternative was sought to allow me to complete the course. I expected more understanding and empathy from them.

The service we received for our weekend rental (Thursday-Sunday) was terrible.
There were problems with the delivery of the motorhome we were assigned because it was in the workshop for maintenance. They got us one, which apparently belonged to the owner's brother-in-law. When we signed the contract and paid the deposit, we had to make our first stop to buy cleaning products because the toilet was dirty with excrement from the previous renter. The next surprise was that the hot water wasn't working because the window that should have been closed had a broken tab. We called them, but they didn't answer, so our second stop was at a campsite. We were traveling with two small children. When my husband finally managed to figure out the problem and "fix" it, it turned out that the vehicle's control display, the one that shows the water percentage, temperature, etc., wasn't working properly, and apparently, there was a sensor under the vehicle that we had to connect. To top it all off, we finally returned the vehicle and they told us they'd process the transfer tomorrow, that we shouldn't worry... that the brother-in-law, who owns the motorhome, is a good guy...
His brother-in-law's company is Karavan Sur Spain.
Oh, and as if that weren't enough, they sent us an audio message saying they'd done us a favor by renting us the motorhome, as they don't rent them out for just 3 days during peak season.
Anyway, anyone thinking of renting should know what to expect. Hope you don't have any problems.

one_star_reviews.text:
Disappointment with the management of Girona Riders at the Sant Gregori BTT school... From our experience, we believe that Girona Riders does not show enough interest or involvement in running the cycling school correctly, especially with regard to the children who compete. We believe that their needs, motivations and concerns are not taken into account enough, and this ends up having a direct impact on them.

The most worrying thing is to see how some children become unmotivated and even end up leaving a sport that they are passionate about. Some have decided to change BTT schools looking for an environment where they feel more listened to, motivated and accompanied.

We are especially sorry because we used to be a big pineapple at the Sant Gregori BTT school, with a very good atmosphere and a lot of enthusiasm. Little by little, however, this pineapple is falling apart, and it is a shame to see how a school that could be a fantastic space for children is losing participants and motivation.

We believe that we should listen much more to families and, above all, to children, and really put their interests and sporting well-being at the center. In the end, the most important thing should be that they enjoy, learn and want to continue cycling.

one_star_reviews.text: At first, everything was wonderful; the service was excellent. I have no complaints about the doctor, who is Colombian and very professional. However, after the initial smile design, the owners kept stringing me along about a veneer repair, which was supposed to be under warranty in less than a month. They kept telling me, "We'll call you, we'll call you, you won't lose the warranty." Three months passed, and they finally made me come in one day. I had to take time off work to travel from Burgos to Madrid, and an hour before the appointment, they texted me saying the doctor was sick and couldn't make it. I texted the doctor, who told me he wasn't sick, had no other appointments scheduled for that day, and was in Seville. Then I asked them why they were lying to me. The owner called to apologize and offered to cover the maintenance, valued at 150 euros, to compensate for the trip and the inconvenience. I agreed, but they kept stringing me along, saying it wouldn't be the same doctor who had treated me initially, but a different one. I told him no, and he said the doctor would see me if I brought him a smile design for someone else to make it worthwhile. I went to a few serious clinics, and in the end, they didn't give me anything for free. They just did the veneer and nothing else. The owner and his managers are liars; they lie to you, they string you along for months and months without giving you an answer, they make you waste your trip, and then they act like they don't know anything. Don't go to this clinic; it's a total scam.

one_star_reviews.text:
My experience with this real estate agency has been terrible, especially considering the price they charge for their services (to both the seller and the buyer).

During the purchase process, I asked the real estate agent three times if I needed to bring any additional documents to the notary. Despite this, they forgot to tell me that I needed one of the documents.

On the day of the signing, they summoned both the buyers and me, as the seller, to the notary's office. Once there, we had to leave without being able to complete the transaction because that document was missing. This meant losing another day of work for everyone involved and having to reschedule the signing.

Furthermore, after they had been advertising the apartment for about two weeks, they pressured me to lower the price, arguing that it would sell quickly. The real estate agency had a two-month exclusivity agreement for the sale of the property, and subsequently sent me a new contract with a lower price, renewing the exclusivity period again, without clearly explaining or informing me that they were extending the exclusivity period. I believe that a modification of this type should have been explained transparently before sending me the contract.

To make matters worse, the private purchase agreement they sent me before I signed it contained numerous errors, including my incorrect email address and the address of the property I was selling. I believe that properly reviewing such an important document should be a basic requirement of any real estate brokerage service.

And all this despite the fact that the agency charged a considerable sum for the entire transaction.

Given the price I paid and the importance of the sale, I expected a much more professional, organized, and transparent service. My experience has been the complete opposite, and I personally would not recommend this agency.

one_star_reviews.text:
⭐ 1 STAR BECAUSE I CAN'T GIVE IT LESS

They've been advertising this gym as being in "pre-opening" for over a year, and finally announced they would open on August 24th. Many users, myself included, trusted that date and canceled our memberships at our usual gyms during August to avoid paying two fees at once.

Well: August 24th came and went, August ended, it's now September 2nd, and the gym still hasn't opened.

The result is that, after making arrangements based on a date they announced, you find yourself without your previous gym and without this one. I find this incredibly unprofessional and a terrible way to treat potential customers.

If you publicly announce an opening date and know that many people will make financial decisions based on it, the least you can do is stick to it, or, if a real problem arises, communicate it well in advance and with complete transparency.

After more than a year of "soft opening," the continued delays and the resulting inconvenience to numerous customers who trusted the announced date have generated very little confidence.

The customer experience has begun even before the official opening, and unfortunately, it couldn't have started worse.

one_star_reviews.text:
I cannot recommend the Recovery Center.

My daughter was admitted here for addiction treatment, and I witnessed two situations that I consider unacceptable in a center supposedly specializing in detoxification:

1. Unlocked medication room. In a center where the patients are people with addiction problems, leaving the medication room open and accessible is not a simple oversight: it's like giving an alcoholic the keys to a bar. It's exactly the kind of negligence that can lead to a serious relapse or worse. A center of this type should have strict security protocols, and this failure demonstrates that Recovery either doesn't have them or doesn't follow them.

2. Unjustified and unjustified expulsion. My daughter was expelled for "misconduct" when, as far as she and I could tell, all she did was defend herself against accusations. Instead of carefully investigating what happened—given that she was a vulnerable patient in the middle of detoxification—the center chose to expel her. And to make matters worse, the person in charge intended to put her in a taxi alone at 8:00 PM, without any accompaniment or supervision from a responsible adult. This is completely irresponsible, especially considering she was in addiction treatment and was in a clearly vulnerable situation at that time.

A center that works with addicts has a special responsibility for care, both in the security of its facilities and in how it manages crises and patient discharges. Recovery failed in both areas. I would not trust this center for the treatment of a family member.

03/09/2026

Response to the center's letter.

Dear Management:

I stand by every point of my review. The deficiencies in the medication custody and the conditions surrounding my daughter's expulsion at 8:00 PM are not mere opinions, but serious facts that directly affected her safety and which I personally witnessed. The protocols of an addiction treatment center are demonstrated through daily rigor, not just on paper. It is regrettable that, faced with legitimate criticism regarding the safety of vulnerable patients, the center's response is self-satisfaction and the suggestion of legal action to try to silence an affected parent. For my part, I have no objection to the records and reports they refer to being reviewed, but by the appropriate authority. I will submit a formal complaint to the Ministry of Health and the Consumer Affairs Office, which are the authorities responsible for evaluating whether their facilities and the management of forced discharges comply with current regulations. My sole objective is to ensure that no other family ever has to endure a similar situation of vulnerability.

Sincerely,

M. Ros

one_star_reviews.text:
I want to document our experience at the Santa Ana residence in Maracena. It has been deplorable from beginning to end. My mother, being a dependent person, has been on the first floor and has been accompanied by us daily; therefore, we have witnessed the poor management of this residence. The lack of staff is undoubtedly what leads to the poor care of the residents. In five months, my mother has had eight falls. One day, we found her on the floor with no staff in the room; another day, we were not informed and found out from another resident's relative; and the last fall caused her significant deterioration. The diaper changes were appalling on numerous occasions, with her being soaked to the floor.

Lack of hydration, lack of attention (being left alone in the room and having to find an assistant because you see that a resident needs help), lack of cleanliness in their room (having to clean their bathroom and chair on many occasions), and finally, poor medical management (we've been to the emergency room because my mother was overmedicated; her checkups weren't properly managed, to the point that we had to check her blood sugar ourselves).
During this period, we filed complaints and held meetings with the director, but nothing changed. We know from other residents that this terrible management has been in place since they opened. In my opinion, I don't recommend it, not even as a last resort.

I brought my motorcycle in to have the spark plug replaced because it wouldn't start.

In conclusion, paying €300 for a €3,000 motorcycle and not even passing the MOT... is, to say the least, regrettable.

That's my experience. I hope you improve in this area.

Best regards.

one_star_reviews.text:
Sad Loss of Trees and Lack of Maintenance

This area used to have a park much loved by the neighborhood, with a large, old tree that, in my opinion, contributed greatly to the environment and landscape.

After the construction of the new Jehovah's Witnesses center, three saplings were planted on the land. These three trees are located on their property, so we neighbors cannot access them to water them or provide any kind of care. Currently, they appear to be completely dead, and at first glance, it seems they haven't received the necessary maintenance.

The contrast is striking between the impeccable appearance of those who attend the center and the desolate state of the surroundings where these three trees are located.

Furthermore, according to the Bible used by Jehovah's Witnesses, Genesis 2:15 speaks of cultivating and caring for a garden. Therefore, as a neighbor, I find it especially sad to see the current condition of these three trees and their surroundings.

I believe it would be desirable to pay more attention to the care and maintenance of these trees, both for the environmental benefit and for the natural heritage of the neighborhood. It's a shame to see how that green space has been lost and how the new trees seem to be in this state.

The tracking number says my order is in the trash. I've called, sent emails, and messaged them on WhatsApp, but I haven't received a response. one_star_reviews.text:
I hired a diagnostic service for an air conditioning unit that was broken, and the initial quote was several thousand euros. This was significantly more expensive than installing a new unit.
Since the damage was covered by insurance, I found it particularly concerning that, after consulting another professional, additional checks were carried out, the real problem was identified, and the unit could be repaired for a considerably lower price.

Personally, the enormous difference between the initial estimate and the final repair cost made me wonder if the fact that an insurance company was initially going to cover the repair might have influenced the price of the solution proposed by ARA.

Furthermore, I received documentation with errors, including an estimate in someone else's name and an invoice with a description that didn't correspond to the work performed. Etc.

The subsequent communication was also very unpleasant, with insistent payment demands and references to legal action, even though I never refused to pay and ultimately made the full payment within a reasonable timeframe.

I was also disappointed by their limited ability to acknowledge and address potential shortcomings in the diagnosis, consistently adopting an overly defensive stance instead of offering clear technical explanations and accepting their share of responsibility.

I strongly advise against working with this company under any circumstances. This review reflects solely my personal experience and is based on the documentation and conversations I have retained.

one_star_reviews.text:
Terrible experience!

I rented an apartment through this real estate agency and it was awful. They rent apartments without knowing their features and provide misleading information. In my case, they advertised it on Idealista with year-round efficient air conditioning, and during the viewing, I asked to confirm it had it and they said yes, so I signed the contract. On my first night in the apartment, the air conditioning turned off at 10 pm, and the next day I notified the real estate agent, who said she would contact them to get it fixed! It turns out that after many days of persistence, I finally managed to speak with the building management. They told me the air conditioning is only on from 10 am to 10 pm, so at night it's like a greenhouse on hot days because it's all windows. When I complained again, they told me they could give me a cheap air conditioner (around €60 from Amazon), another one that would require me to leave the window open and run a hose outside (compromising the insulation), or I could pay for the six months and leave. After continuing to try to terminate the contract due to the deception, I managed to get them to put the property back on the market in exchange for taking an extra month's rent commission (my deposit). They told me that while I was managing it, I naturally kept an eye on the rental to see how it was going because I had to pay it every month and had already spent almost €3,000, including the deposit I was about to lose. To top it all off, on my last call, they told me to stick to the contract, forget about it, and not call them again (Maria Barreras Sanjurjo - the sales agent). (real estate agency), we finally cancelled the agreement and I had no choice but to return to my original contract and stay in the apartment, paying the minimum 6 months stipulated in the contract for that greenhouse apartment!! What a lack of professionalism!!!!!!!!!

one_star_reviews.text:
The experience at this crematorium was very unpleasant. The person who attended to us, Sergio, was arrogant and completely lacked empathy.
Do not choose this crematorium. It's better to choose another one so you can say goodbye to your loved one in a more pleasant environment.

The staff member's behavior was extremely unpleasant from beginning to end.
It's completely unnecessary to answer every question curtly and dismissively. If he dislikes dealing with people, he should find another job, not attend to someone who has just lost a loved one.

When we entered the crematorium room, it was filled with Christian symbols that we hadn't requested. We had to ask more than once for them to be removed, and instead of apologizing for not asking what we wanted, his response was to become defensive, saying that "no one had informed him."

They were finally removed (it didn't take more than five minutes).

VERY NEGATIVE AND WORRYING EXPERIENCE WITH AUTOFURGO GESEMAL 2014 / ENTERPRISE

On the 13th, I rented a vehicle through Autofurgo Gesemal 2014 because my van broke down. As a family of six, I urgently needed a 7-seater vehicle to travel with my wife, four children, and all our luggage.

The reservation was for a Volkswagen Caddy or similar, but Enterprise Ourense gave me a 7-seater automatic Peugeot Rifter. The change of model wasn't the problem.

The problem was that, during the drive from Ourense to Madrid, the vehicle began to swerve and make sudden, abrupt steering movements on its own. I'm not referring to the lane-keeping assist. The behavior seemed abnormal and forced me to drive the entire journey under immense stress, with my wife, four children, and all our luggage inside.

Furthermore, the fuel consumption was very high: approximately €80 worth of diesel for the Ourense-Madrid trip alone.

I reported this and filed a complaint with Enterprise Ourense. The response was that the vehicle "was fine." They also indicated that the car had been delivered to me by an employee who had only recently started working at the company.

Later, I also went to Enterprise Las Rozas to explain what had happened again and seek a solution. The response was once again that the vehicle had no problem.

There is another detail that I found particularly striking: the rental was on the 13th, and on the 14th, at approximately 8:00 a.m., I received a call to assess my experience. I can't say for sure that they were aware of the vehicle's problem beforehand, but, after everything that had happened, it seemed at the very least strange that an assessment was made so soon after and first thing in the morning.

I also filed a complaint with Autofurgo Gesemal 2014, the company through which I arranged the rental. Their written response was that Enterprise billed them for the rental and that if Enterprise accepts my complaint and refunds them, they will also refund me.

Autofurgo also acknowledges that if the vehicle exhibited steering jerks or any other anomaly that could affect safety, Enterprise is responsible for investigating the issue.

The problem is that the customer is caught in the middle: Enterprise refers me to Autofurgo, and Autofurgo is left waiting for Enterprise to resolve the issue and refund them.

I booked and paid for the rental through Autofurgo Gesemal 2014. I don't think it's reasonable that the consumer should have to resolve the financial or billing problems between Autofurgo and Enterprise on their own.

I have already filed the corresponding complaints, and if this isn't resolved, I will pursue the appropriate channels through consumer protection agencies, the OCU (Spanish Consumer Organization), and arbitration.

I am not complaining about the model change. I am filing a complaint because a vehicle exhibited steering behavior that I found abnormal and concerning for safety. I incurred a considerable fuel expense, and after reporting the issue, I have not received a satisfactory solution.

I am not looking for a handout. I am looking for an investigation into what happened and for the appropriate responsibility to be assumed.

After this experience, I do NOT recommend Autofurgo Gesemal 2014 or Enterprise Ourense.

I hope this review will inform other customers about what happened and encourage the companies involved to take seriously complaints related to the safety of the vehicles they provide to their customers.

Two weeks ago today, on Thursday 13th August in Barcelona, I received the wrong delivery: an incorrect colour fridge freezer. It was scheduled for delivery between 09:00 and 15:00, but it didn't arrive until 20:00. The old fridge was also supposed to be taken away as part of the delivery, but the delivery staff said they would only do it if I paid them cash.

Since then, I've been asking MediaMarkt to at least come and remove the incorrect unit, and nothing has been done. I'm now stuck with both my original faulty refrigerator and the incorrect one sitting in my apartment, with no update on when either will be collected, let alone whether I'll get the correct refrigerator or a refund.

Not good enough. The customer service staff have been pleasant, but it's clear they have no authority to actually resolve anything. I would appreciate MediaMarkt actually resolving this rather than more apologies with no action. If this continues much longer, I will be looking into a chargeback through my bank and will never order from MediaMarkt again.

I bought a gold chain that broke almost immediately, without any force or misuse. Their initial solution was to send me to another store to buy the same chain and have the clasp replaced because I didn't like the original. I made it very clear that I didn't want the repaired piece—I didn't want the necklace I was returning—but rather a solution that matched what I had purchased. The response? They gave me the same chain again, repaired, and to top it all off, with a horrible, shoddy, and clearly visible weld.

After paying a significant amount for a new piece of jewelry, I find it shameful and unacceptable to receive a piece with such a poorly done repair, especially after having explicitly stated that I didn't want a new, repaired item.

Very unprofessional and terrible handling of the problem. A real disappointment.

I recommend that you carefully inspect any jewelry before buying it.

one_star_reviews.text:
Deceptive advertising: they abandon you at the slightest complication

On their website, they loudly proclaim: "At La Salud, we will treat you completely free of charge and we will handle everything related to your insurance." The reality is very different. That slogan only holds true if your case is a quick and easy process and the insurance company approves everything on the first try.

The moment your traffic accident case becomes complicated, drags on, or the insurance company starts making bureaucratic excuses not to pay, the hospital comes to a screeching halt. All that promise of "we take care of everything so you only have to think about recovering" vanishes. Instead of mediating with the insurance company as they promise, their administration department washes its hands of the matter and tells you by email that you have to pay for the treatments out of pocket as a private patient and that you should fight the company in court to get your money back.

If you're looking for a medical center that will truly support you administratively against insurance company abuses, this isn't the place. It's a business that only works if the insurance company pays quickly; if there are problems, they leave you completely on your own.
